core.title: Declare a harness type for each acceptance criterion
core.given: An acceptance criterion exists in a plan or acceptance artifact being authored, edited or assessed
core.when: The planner writes, revises or reviews that acceptance criterion
core.then: Ensure the criterion declares a harness type: a code from the harness vocabulary naming the test layer that exercises the acceptance.
prefer: Pick the harness code naming the test layer that actually exercises the acceptance.
Use only codes defined in the harness vocabulary.
avoid: Leaving the harness implicit or undeclared on any acceptance criterion, including pre-existing ones you edit or review.
core.why: The harness tells downstream agents which test layer must exercise the acceptance; without a declared vocabulary code the acceptance cannot be routed to, or proven by, a concrete test.
evidence: Every acceptance criterion in the assessed artifact declares a harness type (in whatever representation the plan format uses) whose value is a code from the harness vocabulary.
No acceptance criterion declares a non-vocabulary harness label.
verification: Term 'harness': the test layer that exercises the acceptance; one of the codes in the stack's harness vocabulary (supplied by the profile). A declared harness value that is not a code in that vocabulary is rejected. The profile value is the authoritative vocabulary itself; codes quoted in the realization are illustrative examples, not the exhaustive membership.
The check is representation-neutral: accept any declaration form the plan format uses to attach a harness type to a criterion; do not require a specific field name.
The observer enumerates every acceptance criterion in the touched or assessed artifact (not only added ones or harness-related diffs) and checks whether each declares a harness type.
Disposition is documentation-only with severity 2: findings are informative, not a strict gate.

values: acceptance criterion present in touched or assessed artifact

fires: The planner adds a new acceptance criterion to a plan.
The planner edits an existing acceptance criterion for any reason (wording, scope, data), including edits unrelated to its harness.
The planner or a reviewer assesses existing acceptance criteria and one of them has no harness type declared.
A harness declaration is changed or removed from an acceptance criterion.
doesNotFire: The planner edits plan prose or docs that contain no acceptance criteria.
The coder changes test implementation files without touching or assessing acceptance definitions.

profileRequirements.meaning: The stack's authoritative harness vocabulary: the codes naming the test layers that can exercise an acceptance criterion. A declared harness type must be a code in that vocabulary; any other label is a non-vocabulary label and is rejected. The profile value names the authoritative vocabulary (or its complete membership); the five codes cited in the Bun realization are illustrative examples of members, not an exhaustive enumeration.
profileRequirements.bunValue: the authoritative harness vocabulary (bun.json cites UNIT, INTEGRATION, HTTP, E2E, SMOKE as illustrative member codes; it does not enumerate the vocabulary's complete membership)

proposedKeys.meaning: The stack's authoritative harness vocabulary: the codes naming the test layers that can exercise an acceptance criterion (the neutral concept 'harness type' that acceptance criteria declare). The profile value identifies the vocabulary and/or its complete membership; codes quoted in rules are illustrative examples.
proposedKeys.bunValue: the authoritative harness vocabulary (illustrative member codes cited: UNIT, INTEGRATION, HTTP, E2E, SMOKE; complete membership not enumerated in bun.json)
proposedKeys.whyNoExistingKey: The idiom group holds the stack's concrete construct for a neutral concept, but no key identifies the harness/test-layer vocabulary used to type acceptance criteria; roles.layers lists architectural layers in dependency order and no other group fits.

bunOnly.reason: Concrete harness codes appear only as an illustrative e.g. list in bun.json; the core states the obligation ('a code from the harness vocabulary') without enumerating, and bun.json remains the worked example. The codes are not the exhaustive vocabulary.

bunOnly.text: e.g. UNIT, INTEGRATION, HTTP, E2E, SMOKE
bunOnly.reason: Same illustrative code list; kept out of the core per the neutral-examples rule.

Concrete rejected labels are instance examples of non-vocabulary labels in the ATDD-Bun harness vocabulary; the core prohibits non-vocabulary labels generically and bun.json remains the worked example.
Same rejected labels as avoid[0]: instance examples of the ATDD-Bun vocabulary with no neutral equivalent beyond 'non-vocabulary harness label'.

bunOnly.text: Positive examples: UNIT, HTTP, E2E, SMOKE (statement also names INTEGRATION). Negative examples (reject): functional, manual.
bunOnly.reason: The term definition and the generic reject rule (any value outside the profile-supplied harness vocabulary) go to core:verification; the concrete positive and negative labels are ATDD-Bun instance examples, and the positive list is explicitly non-exhaustive ('statement also names INTEGRATION').

neutralityNotes: The rule was already representation-neutral (its own verifier_detail[1] forbids requiring a specific declaration form), so the core is near-verbatim. The harness vocabulary is profile-supplied via the proposed key idiom.harness_codes; per audit feedback, bun.json's five codes are treated as illustrative members of the authoritative vocabulary, not an exhaustive enumeration, so instantiation neither rejects valid vocabulary codes nor adds obligations. The illustrative code lists (then, prefer[0], verifier_detail[0] positives) and the concrete rejected labels ('functional', 'manual' in avoid[0], evidence[1], verifier_detail[0] negatives) are carried as bunOnly; bun.json remains the worked example. The fact notes and fires/doesNotFire are preserved (observer scope moved to core:verification; the 'for any reason, not only harness changes' nuance lives in fires). 'unless' is empty in bun.json, so the core has no exceptions and none were added. Per-rule severity and disposition stay in core:verification per the notProfileKeys rule. No detector, validator or finding ids appear in bun.json's agent-facing items, so none needed bunOnly classification.
